scope: Theorem 1.2 (Sharp Gaussian minorants) of the manuscript “An atomic certificate for triangular-lattice universal optimality” (preprints/An-atomic-certificate-for-triangular-lattice-universal-optimality-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 090 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 83e0d874119abae5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every α > 0 there is a real radial Schwartz function fα : R2 → R such that fα(x) ≤ kα(x), ˆ︁ fα(ξ) ≥ 0 (x, ξ ∈ R2 ), and fα(a) = kα(a) (a ∈ A \ {0}), ˆ︁ fα(w) = 0 (w ∈ A∗ \ {0}). For α ≥ 1, the construction uses two finite 20-by-20 interpolation blocks and an absolutely summable infinite correction.
